The author ran the FOCUS Validator without forcing all applicability criteria and noted remaining failures in conditional and composite rules, needing validation-rule or Task Force review. The thread doesn't record an outcome; the pull request was still open.

2673.title: EffectiveCost-C-005-C omits the future-covering qualifier and rejects period-consumed purchases (RM 1.2/1.3)
2673.author: guymano
2673.summary: guymano opened this issue in September 2026. EffectiveCost-C-005-C tests only ChargeCategory Purchase, yet its prose also requires purchases to cover future eligible charges, so a period-consumed subscription fee was flagged on both 1.3.0.1 and 1.2.0.1 when EffectiveCost equalled BilledCost. guymano asked that the rule stop forcing zero on such fees, by keeping the qualifier or classifying the check as dynamic. No outcome is recorded; the issue remains open.

2674.title: ContractApplied property-presence requirements conflict with optional JTD properties and three-key Spend examples after erratum #5
2674.author: guymano
2674.summary: guymano opened this issue on 5 September 2026, reporting a conflict in the ContractApplied rules. Rule CAU-ContractAppliedObject-O-007-M requires all five element keys, including quantity and unit, yet the three-key Spend example (ContractId, ContractCommitmentId, ContractCommitmentAppliedCost) fails it, despite optional JTD properties. guymano said Matt recommended keeping the three-key shape and asked for a consistent shape, model and examples. The thread records no resolution; the issue remains open.

2681.title: [Feedback] Validator/Sample data `ChargeClass != "Correction"` condition never fires when ChargeClass is null
2681.author: qquigley
2681.summary: On 9 September 2026, qquigley reported that fourteen cost and price rules in FOCUS 1.2 to 1.5 can never run. Their guard clause, requiring ChargeClass not equal "Correction", evaluates to null for conformant data, so each rule passes unchecked. A reproduction showed ListCost-C-009-C passing with null ChargeClass but failing with other values. Parallel rules omitting the clause were added in 1.3. The thread records no response and remains open.

2684.title: [AI] Correct non-conformant Constrainable Entity subjects in Tags and AllocatedTags tag key requirements
2684.author: jpradocueva
2684.summary: jpradocueva opened #2684 on 9 September 2026 because several tag key requirements in allocatedtags.md and tags.md use subjects like "User-defined tag key" that aren't on the approved Constrainable Entity list. The suggested fix uses "Tag key" with a "when" condition instead. The issue also raises a guideline ambiguity about whether "user-defined" can qualify a key alone. It remains open, with no decision recorded.

2699.title: [FR] Join cost to usage for work that never became a SKU
2699.author: iwasinnam2
2699.summary: iwasinnam2 asked for a way to join FOCUS cost rows to usage with no SKU, such as gateway replays, without calling it a cache read. On 5 October 2026 Matt-Cowsert asked whether merged rules covered the hit-rate criterion and marked the request needs scoping. On 7 October 2026 iwasinnam2 said they did, planned to add the replay to #2728, and offered to close. The thread doesn't record closure.

2701.title: [AI] Decide the uniqueness scope for identifier columns and apply it consistently
2701.author: Matt-Cowsert
2701.summary: Matt-Cowsert opened this issue on 17 September 2026. Eight identifier requirements, plus CredentialId on #2553, say uniqueness holds within the service provider, but on marketplace rows the principal and credential are assigned under the host provider's model. The issue asked for a decision on the scope, and on whether the change belonged in the 1.5 consistency review or v1.6. The thread has no comments or decision and was still open.

2702.title: [AI] Add a cache cost efficiency query when the SKU Price dataset can supply the uncached input price
2702.author: Matt-Cowsert
2702.summary: Matt-Cowsert opened #2702 on 17 September 2026 to restore a cache cost efficiency query that #2606 removed on 16 September 2026. The query compared caching savings with uncached input cost. Review comments from ijurica and jpradocueva on #2606 raised problems with its price sources and pricing basis. The SKU Price dataset in #2424 does not yet supply uncached input prices. The issue is open, with no decision recorded.

2703.title: [AI] Decide whether JSON columns keep the second link to their schema and apply it consistently
2703.author: Matt-Cowsert
2703.summary: Matt-Cowsert opened this issue on 17 September 2026 to decide whether JSON columns should keep a second, pointer-line link to their schema. Five columns share the pattern. The editorial guidelines and AGENTS.md differ on the repeat, and PR #2514 would drop AGENTS.md's functional-link exemption. jpradocueva suggested removing the pointer link on #2553, which kept it for consistency. The issue is open and no decision is recorded.

2704.title: [Feedback] Clarification Request: Intended HostProviderName and ServiceProviderName Values for Sovereign Clouds (e.g., Azure operated by 21Vianet)
2704.author: jngibert
2704.summary: On 17 September 2026, jngibert asked how HostProviderName and ServiceProviderName apply to sovereign clouds, using Microsoft Azure operated by 21Vianet as the example. They noted the specification's examples do not cover a sovereign brand operated by a separate entity. Three options were posed: Azure as service provider with 21Vianet as host, the reverse, or Azure for both. The thread records no replies and is still open.

2705.title: 1.6 Release Scope / Themes / Milestones
2705.author: Matt-Cowsert
2705.summary: Matt-Cowsert opened this living issue on 21 September 2026 to track proposed scope, themes and milestones for FOCUS 1.6. The description proposes two Core themes with owners: SKU Price dataset generally available (flanakin) and AI dimensions (jerrysr99). Champion work is listed separately. The description was last updated 12 November 2026, and the issue remains open. On 28 September, Matt-Cowsert shared an initial discussion document.

2706.title: [FR] Expose the unit price a commitment discount buys on covered usage
2706.author: Matt-Cowsert
2706.summary: Matt-Cowsert asked on 22 September 2026 for a column showing the per-unit rate a commitment discount produced on covered charges. The issue remained open. A 4 November 2026 status update from Task Force 2 kept it open under #2807 while #2753 was taking shape. Open questions were whether #2753 would cover it and which dataset should carry the rate. Action items went to ijurica, Matt-Cowsert and flanakin.

2707.title: [FR] Define how charges without a unit price are represented
2707.author: Matt-Cowsert
2707.summary: Matt-Cowsert opened this request on 22 September 2026 asking how charges without a unit price should be represented, since several Cost and Usage columns depend on the answer. Working Group members disagreed on whether every charge has a unit price. On 5 October 2026 Matt-Cowsert commented that the request needs scoping before it can move to Under Consideration, retitled it, and recorded a needs-scoping outcome. The issue remains open.

2708.title: [AI] Draft a pull request setting the grain for the AllocatedRatio sum requirement
2708.author: Matt-Cowsert
2708.summary: Matt-Cowsert opened this issue on 22 September 2026 for a draft pull request on the AllocatedRatio sum requirement, which did not state its grain. Graham Murphy reported split allocations summing to 24, because ratios used one time grain while charges were published at another, and proposed the published grain. Irena Jurica moved the grain question to v1.6 or the backlog, which Graham Murphy accepted. The issue stayed open.

2712.title: [FR] Clarify the charge period scope of AllocatedRatio
2712.author: thecloudman
2712.summary: thecloudman opened issue #2712 on 22 September 2026 because the AllocatedRatio requirements do not state what time period the ratio covers. On 29 September 2026, Matt-Cowsert rewrote the problem statement and success criteria. On 8 October 2026, thecloudman was recorded as planning the change for the 1.6 cycle, and pull request #2713 was assigned to them. The issue remains open with no merge recorded.

2713.title: FR #2712: Clarify the charge period scope of AllocatedRatio
2713.author: thecloudman
2713.summary: Pull request #2713, opened as a draft by thecloudman on 22 September 2026, resolves #2712 by stating the charge period over which AllocatedRatio applies. It ties both requirements to the allocated charge's ChargePeriodStart and ChargePeriodEnd and adds an informative note on finer-grained calculation. The author expects the wording may change once #2515 and #2578 settle the origin-row model. The thread is still open and records no outcome.

2715.title: [AI] Align the casing of the Operating Model Conditions label in Content Constraints tables during the 1.5 consistency review
2715.author: Matt-Cowsert
2715.summary: Matt-Cowsert opened #2715 on 22 September 2026 to align the casing of the "Operating Model Conditions" row in Content Constraints tables, which uses title case while other rows use sentence case. A Task Force 1 member spotted it while reviewing #2424, which has the same label. The group agreed to fix it across the specification in the 1.5 consistency review, not on #2424. It remains open with no recorded outcome.

2716.title: [Feedback] Commitment discount examples vary list unit price across scenarios sharing a SkuId
2716.author: Matt-Cowsert
2716.summary: Matt-Cowsert opened this issue on 22 September 2026. It reports that thirteen commitment discount scenario files give one SkuId several ListUnitPrice values, while effective cost is always two thirds of list. Proposed fixes were one list price per SKU, in line with #2711, or a distinct SKU ID per scenario. Pull request #2640 partly addresses it. The issue is still open, and no resolution is recorded.

2717.title: [FR] Clarify JSON format requirements for array-valued columns
2717.author: Matt-Cowsert
2717.summary: Matt-Cowsert opened this request on 22 September 2026, after Requester Details became the first JSON column holding an array. It seeks a unique-key rule so practitioners don't double count cost by key, and wording that covers arrays as well as objects. Options include placing the rule in each column or in the attribute, and rewording, splitting or renaming the attribute. The thread is open, with no outcome recorded.

2721.title: [FR] Enable identifying pricing currency type from FOCUS data
2721.author: Matt-Cowsert
2721.summary: Matt-Cowsert opened this request on 25 September 2026 to find a way to tell from FOCUS data alone whether each Pricing Currency value is a national or consumption currency, since the data doesn't record it. It listed a per-row indicator, a metadata declaration, or a currency reference dataset from #1980 as options. The issue was still open, and the thread recorded no decision.

2722.title: [Maintenance] Validate SQL block columns against the dataset each query reads
2722.author: Matt-Cowsert
2722.summary: Matt-Cowsert opened this issue on 28 September 2026. The SQL block test in specification/tests/test_sql_blocks.py checks columns against one combined list of datasets' columns, so a query can read a column its own table lacks and still pass. This let #2595's queries keep reading replaced columns. The proposed fix checks each column against its table's dataset. The issue is open, and the thread doesn't record the outcome.

2723.title: [Maintenance] Validate SQL block columns against the dataset each query reads
2723.author: Matt-Cowsert
2723.summary: Matt-Cowsert opened #2723 as a draft in September 2026 so the SQL block test checks each column against the dataset its query reads. Before, a query could read a column its table lacked and still pass if another dataset defined it. The change covers aliases, joins and qualified stars, and was verified against open pull requests. The pull request was meant to close #2722 and is still open.

2724.title: [FR] Recognize resellers as price-setting entities
2724.author: ijurica
2724.summary: In September 2026, ijurica asked that FOCUS let a reseller report List pricing from its own price list rather than the SaaS provider's. On 5 October 2026, Matt-Cowsert asked for revised success criteria, since two of three described content rather than outcomes, and linked the request to #2174. The triage outcome was to revise success criteria. The thread doesn't record a final resolution, and the issue remains open.

2728.title: [FR] Map OpenTelemetry attributes to Cost and Usage columns
2728.author: shawnalpay
2728.summary: shawnalpay opened this request on 29 September 2026 to let practitioners join OpenTelemetry telemetry to FOCUS Cost and Usage data without custom tags. On 5 October 2026 shawnalpay and samrogowicz presented to Semantic Conventions SIG, which advised a separate repository. On 7 October 2026 iwasinnam2 suggested gateway replay as a use case. On 2 November 2026 Matt-Cowsert requested revisions to the title, success criteria, priorities and scope. It remains open.

2729.title: [FR] Clarify key casing in custom columns
2729.author: Matt-Cowsert
2729.summary: Matt-Cowsert opened this feature request on 29 September 2026. It asks whether keys in custom key-value columns keep their native casing, and what data generators should do with keys they introduce. The request follows a question raised in #2322. Existing requirements on fidelity and string handling don't settle whether keys count as values. The thread records no comments or decision, and the issue remains open.

2730.title: [FR] Enable magnitude abbreviations in Unit Format
2730.author: Matt-Cowsert
2730.summary: Matt-Cowsert opened this request on 29 September 2026, asking that Unit Format allow magnitude abbreviations. Unit Format accepts only whole numbers, so token prices appear as "1000000 Tokens", which is hard to read. The request cites AWS and Azure price lists using "1K" and "1M". On 22 September 2026, Task Force 1 agreed to allow K, M, B and T abbreviations. The issue remains open, and its description is truncated.

2733.title: [FR] Add pricing block size
2733.author: Matt-Cowsert
2733.summary: Matt-Cowsert opened this request on 29 September 2026 for a pricing block size column. Providers often price blocks, such as per 100 hours, but FOCUS carries the block size only within the pricing unit, so practitioners must parse and rescale prices by hand. Microsoft and Google handle block sizes differently. A contributor on #2424 agreed a column would help. The issue is open, and the thread records no decision.

2735.title: [AI] Align the SKU Price record wording across the SKU Price dataset
2735.author: Matt-Cowsert
2735.summary: Matt-Cowsert opened this issue on 30 September 2026 to fix six lines in the SKU Price dataset and examples that call a single record the SKU Price, per #2725. It proposed "SKU Price record" in informative text and "SkuPrice record" in requirements. A 26 October 2026 comment by Matt-Cowsert said maintainers agreed to defer the work to the 1.6 cycle instead of the 1.5 review. The issue was still open.

2737.title: [AI] Define conventions for cross-dataset normative requirements
2737.author: ijurica
2737.summary: On 1 October 2026 ijurica opened #2737 to define conventions for cross-dataset requirements, since the guidelines don't cover six existing comparisons. Proposed: a DatasetId.ColumnId reference form, canonical row-level and aggregate patterns, explicit nullable join keys, a rule that such requirements apply only when the counterpart exists, and a verb for Date/Time equality. It was linked to #2237 as a possible parent. The thread doesn't record the outcome; it remains open.

2739.title: [FR] Add tier application model for quantity tier pricing
2739.author: Matt-Cowsert
2739.summary: Matt-Cowsert opened this request on 2 October 2026, asking that the SKU Price dataset state whether a price's quantity tiers are graduated, with each tier's rate covering only its own units, or volume-style, with the reached tier's rate covering all units. On #2424, a separate column was suggested for tracking in a future release. The issue remains open and the thread records no decision.

2741.title: [FR] Identify the discounts applied to a charge
2741.author: Matt-Cowsert
2741.summary: Matt-Cowsert opened this issue on 5 October 2026 to identify every discount applied to a charge beyond commitment discounts, such as negotiated or bundled ones. Practitioners now infer discount mechanisms from several columns, and when two discounts overlap, only the commitment is identified. The proposal is to evaluate a discount type column, building on #2642. It carries over from closed #1037. The issue is open, with no discussion recorded.

2742.title: [FR] Enable comparing commitment discounts with on-demand rates
2742.author: Matt-Cowsert
2742.summary: Matt-Cowsert opened #2742 on 6 October 2026 because FOCUS price data cannot show the rate a commitment discount produces, so it cannot be compared with on-demand rates. They later listed four missing pieces, including a link from purchase to covered usage. Draft #2753 tests one approach, and Irena Jurica leads the work. The issue remains open.

2743.title: [FR] Clarify cross-record requirements under appended corrections
2743.author: Matt-Cowsert
2743.summary: Matt-Cowsert opened this request on 6 October 2026 after review of #2567. Practitioners cannot tell which record carries the value in effect after a Delta or Ledger correction, because cross-record requirements do not say which records they cover. ijurica proposed identifying corrections and linking them to originals in Correction Handling. Task Force 1 moved the question here so #2567 could proceed. The thread doesn't record the outcome; it remains open.

2745.title: [FR] Add contract identification to Cost and Usage charges
2745.author: Matt-Cowsert
2745.summary: Matt-Cowsert opened a request on 6 October 2026 asking Cost and Usage to identify the contract that set each negotiated price, even without a commitment. The existing contract identifier, Contract Applied, is conditional and may be absent for such charges. The gap blocks matching charges to SKU Price records in #2424. CloudVane and the FinOps Foundation registered support. The thread records no decision and remains open.

2746.title: [FR] Clarify null handling for details columns
2746.author: Matt-Cowsert
2746.summary: Matt-Cowsert opened this request on 6 October 2026 because each details column sets its own null rule. Task Force 2 agreed on 30 September 2026 that this needed its own request. Udam Dewaraja asked on #2553 why details would be required when a generator has identifiers but no details. Irena Jurica found the differing rules acceptable, given that the columns differ in importance. The request remains open.

2748.title: AI #2364: Add `QuantityTierCategory` to `SkuPrice` dataset
2748.author: shawnalpay
2748.summary: shawnalpay proposed adding a QuantityTierCategory column to SKU Price, with allowed values Graduated or Retroactive, so tiered pricing can be calculated correctly. mike-finopsorg, jpradocueva and jerrysr99 approved. On 16 November 2026, Matt-Cowsert requested wording, version, example and rebase changes. The pull request was still open.

2749.title: AI #2364: Add `SkuMeter` to `SkuPrice` dataset
2749.author: shawnalpay
2749.summary: shawnalpay opened #2749 to add a mandatory, nullable SkuMeter column to the SKU Price dataset, mirroring the existing Cost and Usage column so practitioners can filter price catalogs by meter without custom x_ columns. jpradocueva, flanakin and jerrysr99 approved. Matt-Cowsert suggested rewording, a consistency-rule fix, a preview version label, and raised example CSVs and rebasing. FR #2807 questions where SkuMeter belongs. The PR remains open.

2753.title: FOCUS #2751: Adding CommitmentApplicability to the SKU Price dataset
2753.author: ijurica
2753.summary: Pull request #2753, opened by ijurica on 8 October 2026, proposed a CommitmentApplicability column on commitment purchase records instead of separate usage records. It argued a commitment price is a different amount for the same SKU Price, not a new SKU Price. On 5 November 2026, Matt-Cowsert assigned ijurica a TF2 action item to present the approach and its size impact. The thread doesn't record the outcome; it remains open.

2759.title: Maintenance #2758: Add Display Name casing lint rule and automatic lint fixes
2759.author: finops-DaveMoreau
2759.summary: finops-DaveMoreau opened this draft pull request on 9 October 2026 to close #2758. It adds lint rule MD992, which checks and auto-fixes Display Name casing in column file introductions, plus tooling such as make lint-fix and pre-commit hooks. On 12 October 2026, ijurica asked that the rule first be added to the editorial guidelines and that the team agree how custom lint rules are tested. The thread is still open.

2760.title: [AI] Remove leading articles from column introduction subjects
2760.author: finops-DaveMoreau
2760.summary: Issue #2760, opened by finops-DaveMoreau on 9 October 2026, proposed that column introductions begin with the Display Name, without an article. Of 126 such introductions, 28 use one, which the author says makes the name read as a common noun. The proposal would add a rule to the editorial guidelines and remove those articles. It relates to #2740 and #2758. The thread doesn't record the outcome; the issue is open.

2761.title: [FR] Define preview status for new FOCUS content
2761.author: Matt-Cowsert
2761.summary: FR #2761 asked for a preview status for new FOCUS content that is approved but may change. shawnalpay raised questions on a draft, and reviewers then covered PR #2762, which defines preview for whole datasets. Matt-Cowsert approved it on 19 October 2026. Members approved preview for SKU Price in PR #2752 in October 2026. Preview work moved to FR #2782, and PR #2776 was held for 1.6. It remains open.

2763.title: [AI] Add FOCUS 1.4 support to the hosted FOCUS Validator
2763.author: Matt-Cowsert
2763.summary: Matt-Cowsert asked that the hosted FOCUS Validator add v1.4, matching the open-source focus-validator 2.2.1 package (#1984). The request also covered Invoice Detail and Billing Period datasets and outdated "(1.2 or 1.3)" text. On 14 October 2026 Matt-Cowsert reported that 2.2.1 crashes on the 1.4 model and asked mike-finopsorg to confirm the hosted tool uses the 1.4.0.1 prerelease model or a fix. It remains open with no recorded outcome.

2768.title: [AI] Track the open questions for the SKU Price dataset
2768.author: Matt-Cowsert
2768.summary: Matt-Cowsert opened this issue on 13 October 2026 to track the SKU Price dataset as a preview. Members chose that path on 22 October 2026, and #2752 applies the label, pending final approval on 29 October 2026. Four open questions, raised by flanakin and ijurica, were listed, along with conformance exclusions. The issue remains open; unchecked tasks include early implementers, the next decision date and answers to the questions.

2769.title: [AI] Define review artifacts for content held back from a release
2769.author: Matt-Cowsert
2769.summary: Matt-Cowsert opened this issue on 14 October 2026, proposing that the SKU Price branch from PR #2424 be released as a separate, watermarked review artifact outside FOCUS 1.5, with guidelines for approval, labeling, distribution and retirement. The checklist asked for a comparison with the preview proposal in PR #2762 and for rules on choosing between stable, preview and review-artifact publication. The issue remains open, and the thread records no outcome.

2770.title: AI #2769: Define review artifact process
2770.author: Matt-Cowsert
2770.summary: Matt-Cowsert proposes guidelines for review artifacts: watermarked PDFs that share content held back from a FOCUS release, so data generators and practitioners can give feedback without it being a release or for production use. The first use would be the SKU Price dataset (#2424), kept out of FOCUS 1.5 and shared separately, a third option beside the preview path in #2762 and #2752. The guidelines set conditions for approval, faithfulness, fixed builds, labeling and clearance. Little reaction shows so far; the latest activity is Matt-Cowsert's 11 November 2026 note that foundation #38 merged on 22 October 2026, adding section 5.3 to the Operating Procedures, so the guidelines no longer wait on Steering Committee ratification. Matt-Cowsert has asked for another look, so the thread looks to be waiting on Members' feedback.

2776.title: Label Version Introduced with GA
2776.author: flanakin
2776.summary: flanakin proposed an editorial change prefixing every Version Introduced value with a GA label, matching the Preview and GA format from #2762. Matt-Cowsert asked how content first published in 0.5 and 1.0-preview should be labelled, which flanakin considered implicitly preview, and in October 2026 said the change did not clearly suit consistency review. It remains an open draft pull request.

2778.title: AI #2572: Update the editorial guidelines for section heading naming and supported column coverage
2778.author: Matt-Cowsert
2778.summary: Matt-Cowsert opened this pull request to add editorial guidelines on section headings and column coverage, as #2572 asked. Headings count as non-normative, so existing Display Name rules apply, and listed columns must appear in an example query. Three rules came from #2766. ijurica's review asked for less duplication, which Matt-Cowsert addressed on 28 October 2026. The PR moved to the 1.6 cycle and stayed in draft. It remains open.

2779.title: [FR] Enable verifiable entity references in specification source
2779.author: finops-DaveMoreau
2779.summary: finops-DaveMoreau proposed verifiable entity references in the specification source, so that each reference names its column, glossary term or other entity and a check reports mismatches in each pull request. They built a prototype on a branch, with no pull request yet. Matt-Cowsert edited the issue for triage, asking finops-DaveMoreau to confirm seven changes. The thread doesn't record a confirmation. The issue is still open.

2780.title: AI #2698: Drop Version Updated from supported features
2780.author: finops-DaveMoreau
2780.summary: In October 2026 finops-DaveMoreau opened pull request #2780 to resolve #2698 by removing the Version Updated section from four supported features and adding a guideline rule barring it from entity and supported feature sections. The author noted that only four of 227 files use the field and offered keeping it with selective use as an alternative. Matt-Cowsert approved, asking that the rule name supported features explicitly. jpradocueva and ijurica said unrelated validation findings belonged in a separate editorial pull request. thecloudman declined to approve, wanting version markers on learning material such as queries. On 28 October 2026 Matt-Cowsert said the team would leave things as they are, use this as a primary application point in 1.6, and remove the pull request from the 1.5 milestone. It remains open.

2782.title: [FR] Define the preview lifecycle for whole datasets
2782.author: Matt-Cowsert
2782.summary: The issue asks for the rest of the preview lifecycle for whole datasets, which PR #2762 left open. Practitioners need to know which FOCUS content is preview and what it takes to become stable before building on it. Matt-Cowsert is drafting PR #2843 to set these rules. The 17 November update records agreement that a preview's scope list names only entities that exist for the preview, that features depending on preview content are also preview, and that new datasets start as preview but can go straight to general availability when evidence is strong. Glossary wording, requirement checks and Version Introduced remain open. Alex Hullah raised a concern that a preview label could reduce implementer feedback, which Matt-Cowsert said is not zero. The PR left draft on 16 November, and the 1.6 deadline still applies.

2783.title: [Feedback] `CAU-CommitmentDiscountStatus-C-005-M` and `CAU-CommitmentDiscountCategory-C-005-M`: no Condition, so null fails the allowed values (contradicts `C-003-C`)
2783.author: wjesseclements
2783.summary: On 21 October 2026, wjesseclements reported that the CommitmentDiscountStatus and CommitmentDiscountCategory allowed-values rules (C-005-M) have no condition, so nulls fail them. This contradicts C-003-C, which requires null when there is no commitment discount. Proposed fixes were a not-null condition on each rule, or moving the wording under a not-null clause as sibling columns do. The thread records no response, and the issue remains open.

2786.title: [FR] Align supported features with the use case library
2786.author: Matt-Cowsert
2786.summary: Matt-Cowsert opened this request on 23 October 2026, asking that supported feature queries and the use case library be aligned. They noted that 20 of 43 specification queries appear as copies in the library, seven 1.4 use cases carry pre-1.4 values, and the two sets diverge. The proposal maps use cases to supported features by specification names and refreshes copies at ratification. The thread records no outcome; it remains open.

2796.title: [AI] Define how glossary terms are referenced outside the glossary
2796.author: ijurica
2796.summary: ijurica opened #2796 on 27 October 2026 asking whether FOCUS specification sections may restate a glossary term's definition instead of linking to it. The issue cites billing currency, service name and SKU price sections, whose introductions repeat glossary wording. The proposal is an editorial guideline on glossary references, then a separate review of affected sections. The issue is still open and records no outcome.

2800.title: [AI]  Plan around 1.5 Preview Material - outbound and inbound
2800.author: beau-finopsorg
2800.summary: This is a planning issue, opened by beau-finopsorg on 27 October 2026, asking for a plan covering what to share about the FOCUS 1.5 SKU Price Sheet Dataset Preview, when to share it, and what data to gather around it, both outbound and inbound. The description adds nothing beyond that goal, so the thread holds no draft plan yet. The only recent activity is one comment from Matt-Cowsert on 17 November 2026 saying they and beau-finopsorg will talk it through in their one-to-one. No one else has weighed in, and no options or positions are on record, so there is no visible sign yet of support or disagreement. The issue remains open and appears to be waiting on that conversation. Anyone outside it would need a written plan in the thread before they could see what is proposed.

2805.title: [FR] Represent AI reasoning level in usage data
2805.author: turso77
2805.summary: turso77 opened a feature request on 29 October 2026 for a standard FOCUS field for AI reasoning level, since it affects cost and performance but isn't consistently reported. Matt-Cowsert's triage on 31 October asked for a revised use case and criteria, dropped performance, and asked whether the level belongs in FOCUS data or in joined request records (#2728). MasonSalisbury argued for the data itself. The issue was still open.

2807.title: [FR] Promote the SKU Price dataset to general availability
2807.author: Matt-Cowsert
2807.summary: This thread tracks moving the SKU Price dataset out of preview, so its requirements count toward conformance and its shape follows normal deprecation rules. The FinOps Foundation rates it nice to have, and the #1057 requesters are invited to add support. Task Force 2 on 11 November kept PR #2845's wording and moved the row-versus-record question to #1027. @flanakin's draft in #2826 would let users pull only changed records, which matters for dataset size. Open questions remain on SkuMeter, the primary key and the name. The Maintainers on 16 November made no decision on renaming: Irena Jurica argues SKU Price blurs the identifier and the dataset, while others doubt the concern is clear. Task Force 2 revisits the name on 18 November, so general availability looks some way off.

2811.title: [FR] Clarify preview status changes for whole datasets
2811.author: Matt-Cowsert
2811.summary: Matt-Cowsert opened this on 1 November 2026 to settle questions 3 and 7 from FR #2782: what happens to scope-list items when a whole preview dataset is promoted or removed, and how the requirements model shows Preview status. No proposal covers removal. On 3 November 2026, TF1 noted the 1.5 requirements model omits preview; Matt-Cowsert said it must accept Preview by the end of the 1.6 cycle. It remains open.

2816.title: [FR] Define what version sections record for FOCUS content
2816.author: Matt-Cowsert
2816.summary: Matt-Cowsert opened this feature request on 3 November 2026 so practitioners can tell which version added or last changed a column or supported feature. The request says Version Introduced and Version Updated lack a defined meaning, leading to values like 0.5 for beta content and different values for one column across datasets. It links draft PR #2776 and PR #2780, both held for 1.6. The issue remains open.

2817.title: [AI] Draft a first model of context window pricing for FR 2521
2817.author: Matt-Cowsert
2817.summary: Matt-Cowsert opened the issue on 3 November 2026 to draft a first model of context window size pricing for FR #2521. Tasks included checking the FR against provider pricing and placing the property in the Cost and Usage dataset, possibly as an SKU Price column. jerrysr99 reported 24 models from six providers using two price bands and asked whether two are enough. The thread records no outcome and remains open.

2819.title: FR #2779: Tag entity references semantically across the specification
2819.author: finops-DaveMoreau
2819.summary: On 3 November 2026 finops-DaveMoreau opened draft pull request #2819, resolving #2779, to tag references to entities semantically across the specification instead of relying on formatting. A build resolver turns the tags into ordinary Markdown, and a generated registry checks them, reporting inconsistencies rather than fixing them. No review outcome is recorded. The pull request is still open, awaiting Working Group decisions on several questions.

2820.title: [FR] Demonstrate reusable scope rule evaluation in supported features
2820.author: ijurica
2820.summary: The request asks for a complete, reusable evaluation of the scope rules shared by eligibility and applicability columns, so data engineers need not derive it from the processing workflow. Today SKU Price Eligibility queries evaluate only part of the rules, and no supported feature uses Contract Commitment Applicability. Replying to triage feedback from Matt-Cowsert, ijurica narrowed 'reusable' to reuse across supported features rather than across columns, with one non-normative evaluation per column. In scope are SKU Price Eligibility and Contract Commitment Applicability; the draft column from #2753 is optional. Edge cases such as In and NotIn on a null dimension, which the applicability definition does not cover, remain an open question. No one else has commented yet, so support is untested; the author will revise the problem statement, use case and success criteria to match.

2821.title: [Feedback] Replace undefined Entry references in Requester Details object requirements
2821.author: Matt-Cowsert
2821.summary: Matt-Cowsert opened this issue on 4 November 2026 because the Requester Details requirements use "Entry", which the specification never defines. The proposal swaps these for paths starting from RequesterDetailsObject, matching other columns, without changing the data shape or constraints. Matt-Cowsert says this would let validators use only dataset facts. The Requirements Model meeting discussed it on 3 November 2026. The issue remains open within the 1.5 errata bundle.

2826.title: Add changed-since configuration to SKU Price dataset
2826.author: flanakin
2826.summary: flanakin opened this pull request on 4 November 2026 to let SKU Price deliveries include only prices changed since a chosen point in time. The reason given was size: re-sending every row monthly would be about 7.5 GB, versus 0.64 GB for changes only. On 18 November 2026, flanakin pushed revisions covering Append delivery, key-changing corrections, scheduled cutoffs and retirements. The PR remained open, with no reviewer comments recorded.

2831.title: [AI] Line up practitioners to review SKU Price sample data
2831.author: Matt-Cowsert
2831.summary: Matt-Cowsert opened this issue on 5 November 2026, following Task Force 2's 4 November 2026 agreement to recruit practitioners to review SKU Price sample data once available. Their feedback would inform open questions in #2768. Reviewers would be asked whether they would use spot prices. The thread says spot pricing is not needed for general availability. The issue remains open, and the thread doesn't record any agreed reviewers.

2832.title: [Editorial] Correct the Contract Commitment and commitment program examples for the 1.5 release
2832.author: Matt-Cowsert
2832.summary: Matt-Cowsert opened this issue on 5 November 2026 after a reviewer checked the 1.5 specification. It lists wrong examples, example data, and descriptions in the contract commitment and commitment program eligibility text, including invalid category values, a discount formula, and period dates. The editorial fixes aim to merge before the 1.5 IP Review ends on 1 December 2026. No comments or decisions are recorded, and the issue is open.

2833.title: [Editorial] Correct the split cost allocation and commitment discount examples for the 1.5 release
2833.author: Matt-Cowsert
2833.summary: Matt-Cowsert opened this issue on 5 November 2026 to collect errors in 1.5 appendix examples found during a 4 November review. The proposed fixes covered commitment discount and split cost allocation numbers, a ServiceSubcategory value, a null origin-row field, and two supported feature queries. They were meant to merge before the review ended on 1 December 2026. The issue was open, and the thread doesn't record the outcome.

2834.title: [Editorial] Correct the metadata links, key names, and examples for the 1.5 release
2834.author: Matt-Cowsert
2834.summary: Matt-Cowsert opened this issue on 5 November 2026 to fix errors in the 1.5 Metadata section and examples, found in a 4 November review. Fixes cover broken links, wrong key names, a nonexistent Contract dataset, and timestamp format. Changes are informative only and may merge into working_draft before the IP Review ends 1 December 2026. Requirement-text fixes are proposed in #2836 and #2837. No decisions recorded; the issue remains open.

2835.title: [Editorial] Correct summary tables, glossary entries, labels, and links for the 1.5 release
2835.author: Matt-Cowsert
2835.summary: Matt-Cowsert opened this editorial issue on 5 November 2026 to list errors found in a review of the 1.5 specification. Fixes covered summary tables, glossary entries and order, preview labels, relationships, section order and links. Text-only fixes were to merge into working_draft before the IP Review's end on 1 December 2026. Requirement-text fixes were proposed as errata in #2836. The thread records no discussion, and the issue was open.

2836.title: [Feedback] Correct casing, IDs, and links in 1.5 requirement text
2836.author: Matt-Cowsert
2836.summary: This issue, opened by Matt-Cowsert, collects nine fixes from a review of the full 1.5 specification: casing errors such as 'MUST not' and SchemaID, one link pointing at the wrong InvoiceId, and a renamed condition. None changes what a requirement asks for. The description planned to hold them for the 1.5 release as errata. The only later activity is a comment by Matt-Cowsert saying maintainers agreed to apply them now as an editorial improvement targeting working_draft, so they no longer seem to be waiting for the release. That comment dates the meeting 2027, which looks like a slip for 2026. The renamed condition in row 9 needs care, since it changes a published anchor and eleven links, and the comment does not say whether it was kept. No one else has replied, so support or objections are not yet visible.

2837.title: [Feedback] Correct the Payment Currency, Contract ID, and Time Sector End requirements
2837.author: Matt-Cowsert
2837.summary: Matt-Cowsert opened this issue on 5 November 2026 to log three requirement fixes from a 1.5 specification review. The fixes add a Currency Format requirement to PaymentCurrency, remove a redundant ContractId condition, and change a lowercase "must" in TimeSectorEnd to MUST. The Maintainers must decide whether each is an erratum or a feature request. The thread records no decision, and the issue is still open.

2838.title: [Maintenance] State how repeated [*] paths bind to array elements in JSON object requirements
2838.author: finops-DaveMoreau
2838.summary: The issue asks how repeated [*] paths in JSON Object requirements bind to array elements. finops-DaveMoreau notes the guidelines don't say whether a second [*] path means the same element as the first, and RFC 9535 would allow either reading. The affected requirements fall into four groups: some where the same element is clearly meant but unstated, one where different elements are meant (scope tied to #2701), one where a [*] subject conflicts with "for one object", and a minor missing-location case. The proposed fix is an explicit qualifier in each requirement. Matt-Cowsert reports that #2827 now uses plain back-references instead of "in the same entry", and asks that four Requester Details lines join the same-element table. No replies yet; the issue remains open.

2839.title: [FR] Clarify Tier and Tiered Terminology in the Specification
2839.author: ijurica
2839.summary: Opened by ijurica on 5 November 2026, #2839 asks that the specification use "tier" and "tiered" consistently across pricing thresholds, commitment discounts, storage tiers and SaaS feature tiers. The minimum proposal adds glossary terms for tiered pricing and rewords ambiguous mentions to link to them. It cites the unmerged #2564 as earlier work. The issue is open, and the thread doesn't record an outcome.

2840.title: AI #2825: Add 1.5 Changelog
2840.author: Matt-Cowsert
2840.summary: Matt-Cowsert's PR adds the v1.5 section to CHANGELOG.md, built from the diff between the v1.4 tag and v1.5-cr rather than milestone titles. It is part of #2825 and does not close it, as the Contributors list is still separate. The main judgement calls are six Migration Compatible changes, where queries or ingestion may need updating, such as the price redefinition, consumption currency and ContractedUnitPrice presence. shawnalpay confirmed the counts and raised classification and wording questions, which Matt-Cowsert has addressed in later commits. Six approvals are recorded by 19 November, and no change requests are shown. Entries for the IP Review editorial fixes will follow as they merge; #2836 and #2837 are excluded as post-release errata. It looks close to ready ahead of the 3 December 2026 WG approval date.

2841.title: [AI] Add 1.4 to 1.5 version migration guidance
2841.author: Matt-Cowsert
2841.summary: Matt-Cowsert asks for a FOCUS 1.4 to 1.5 section in the version migration guidance, modelled on the 1.3 to 1.4 section (#1548, #1597) and placed above it. It would be built from the v1.5 changelog (#2840) and a diff between the published 1.4 spec and the 1.5 release candidate. For people producing or consuming FOCUS data, it would cover each Migration Compatible change, the operating model conditions now governing column presence, and renames to the anchor and requirements models that affect tooling. It would also state that the SKU Price preview is excluded from conformance. The target is a pull request approved by Members before the working group approves v1.5 on 3 December 2026. No one has replied yet, so support or objections are unknown, and the thread looks quiet since opening on 6 November 2026.

2842.title: AI #2841: Add 1.4 to 1.5 migration guide
2842.author: Matt-Cowsert
2842.summary: This pull request adds a 1.4 to 1.5 migration section to the version migration guidance, implementing #2841 ahead of the planned v1.5 approval. The main point is that 1.5 removes and renames no columns, so the impact is on values, such as how List, Contracted and Effective Cost relate. ijurica, reviewing the negotiated pricing wording, suggested limiting the gap to Effective Cost to discount-bearing commitment programs and placing non-discount negotiated terms in Contracted Cost; Matt-Cowsert applied both in c72bbe8b. ijurica also sees most unit price and cost changes as clarifications rather than substantive change and questioned a sentence on List Cost; Matt-Cowsert dropped that clause and invited alternative wording. A milestone mismatch was raised and explained as intentional. No approvals are recorded, and the List Cost wording remains open.

2843.title: FR #2782: Define the preview lifecycle for whole datasets
2843.author: Matt-Cowsert
2843.summary: Matt-Cowsert opened this draft pull request as a starting point for feature request #2782, which asks how a whole-dataset preview moves to stable or is removed, since the merged rules only cover its start. It adds markers to the Preview Process in the spec change guidelines: Proposed answers where existing evidence supports one, and TODO markers elsewhere. Proposals cover supporting entities, the scope list rule for requirements, and which Version Introduced value shows after promotion, and drafted text covers four questions. Nothing merges until the Task Force settles each answer. No approvals, change requests or comments are recorded yet, so reaction is not visible. The description says Task Force 1 took it up on 10 November 2026, but the record shows the change to TF-Core 1 that day, so its placement looks unsettled.

2844.title: [AI] Create the FOCUS 1.5 Data Model spreadsheet
2844.author: Matt-Cowsert
2844.summary: Matt-Cowsert opened this action item to produce the FOCUS 1.5 Data Model spreadsheet, the filterable file listing every dataset and column, which the website still links only for 1.4. It is built from the 1.5 release candidate and adds the preview SKU Price dataset (23 columns), four Cost and Usage columns, and operating model conditions replacing free-text conditions and the Applicability Criteria tab. Two of those conditions are also preview, and some allowed values change, such as ServiceSubcategory gaining Bare Metal. A draft exists but will be rebuilt from the release tag after ratification. Maintainers must still settle choices the specification leaves open, such as column categories and whether to keep shortened descriptions. It moved to In Progress on 10 November 2026, due 17 November 2026, and no one has commented yet.

2845.title: AI #2735: Align SKU Price record wording across the SKU Price dataset
2845.author: finops-DaveMoreau
2845.summary: finops-DaveMoreau opened #2845 to close #2735 by changing six SKU Price dataset lines to name the record, since eligibility can differ between records. Because the dataset shares the construct's name, they proposed renaming it. ijurica approved on 11 November 2026, flagging a release mismatch. TF2 agreed the PR lands in 1.6. The thread doesn't record a merge, and the PR was still open at its last comment.

2846.title: Editorial #2832: Correct the Contract Commitment and commitment program examples
2846.author: Matt-Cowsert
2846.summary: This pull request corrects examples in the Contract Commitment and Commitment Program Eligibility Details text that don't match allowed values or requirements, closing #2832. Fixes include allowed ServiceCategory and ServiceSubcategory values, the UsageType and CDN filters, the discount percentage formula, and merging StackLens's monthly and annual programs into one Interval Spend Commitment. No requirement lines change. The main point under discussion was what Interval Spend Commitment means. ijurica read the monthly and annual intervals as resetting minimums, which conflicted with a Full Period row. Matt-Cowsert agreed and changed that row to Monthly. kk09v and jpradocueva approved. kk09v's question on the Datadog reference and Flexible Spend Plan was answered in-thread. Last activity was 19 November 2026, with Matt-Cowsert saying they would make the line 65 change too. No merge is recorded.

2849.title: [AI] Track the 1.5 errata from Maintainer assessment to one errata PR
2849.author: Matt-Cowsert
2849.summary: This Action Item tracks the 1.5 errata candidates, filed as separate Feedback issues, from Maintainer assessment to one errata PR against working_draft, merged after 1.5 is published. Three are listed: #2836 corrects casing, IDs and links in 1.5 requirement text; #2837 corrects the PaymentCurrency, ContractId and TimeSectorEnd requirements; and #2783 points out that two CAU commitment discount requirements have no Condition, so a null value fails them, also in 1.2 to 1.4. Under the Errata Guidelines, changes to BCP-14 keywords, added columns or properties, or validation logic go to Feature Request instead. An open question is whether SkuPrice rules should join the 1.5 model through errata. The thread was opened by Matt-Cowsert on 10 November 2026 with no comments or assessments yet, so support can't be judged; all three candidates still await Maintainer assessment.

2850.title: [AI] Compare SKU Price dataset columns with SkuPriceDetails properties
2850.author: Matt-Cowsert
2850.summary: This issue asks for a two-way check of SKU Price dataset columns against FOCUS-defined SkuPriceDetails properties. It follows a TF1 discussion: SkuPriceDetails is meant to describe what matters for a SKU, not its price tiers, yet context window size sits apart from AI properties such as model family. jerrysr99 posted the comparison on 16 November, listing 25 SKU Price columns and 21 properties, with only the two context window bounds from #2521 appearing in both. The list is a snapshot; it does not yet say which gaps should close, and no one has responded since. If the group proceeds, Matt-Cowsert expects one feature request per column added, as with the model family and token direction properties. One participant warned that carrying every column would keep SkuPriceDetails growing. Results go to TF1 on 17 November.

2851.title: [AI] Reword "term" in the Commitment Discount Quantity requirement
2851.author: Matt-Cowsert
2851.summary: Matt-Cowsert opened this issue after a #2773 review found that "term" in the Commitment Discount Quantity requirement is ambiguous. It means how long the commitment discount runs, which the introduction calls its period, yet the glossary defines Term as an agreement on a contract or invoice. A reviewer removed the glossary link, but the wording stayed because rewording a normative requirement was out of scope for an editorial PR. The options are keeping "term" as plain English, or rewording it to "period", the closer fit, which changes requirement text. That means it cannot merge into the working draft during the 1.5 IP Review, so it moves to the 1.6 cycle. The first step searches the specification for other requirements using "term" for a duration. No one has commented yet, so the group's leaning is unclear.

2852.title: [AI] Decide how the Columns table and the Requirements column list count for first-occurrence linking

The open choices are whether the table counts, which would make the list link the repeat, and whether the list needs its own exception, since linking every column there is existing practice. 2854.title: [AI] Revisit the SKU Price Description column

2854.summary: ijurica opened this issue because the introduction and Description section of the SKU Price Description column conflict over whether it describes the SKU Price construct or a single SKU Price record. Choosing the construct reading raises further questions about whether descriptions must match across records of one ID and differ between IDs of the same provider. Rewording alone would not settle it, since the column is described as self-contained and as adding information not otherwise available. For producers and users of FOCUS data, the answer changes what a value describes. Nobody has responded since opening on 11 November 2026, so support is unclear.

2855.title: [AI] Align pricing terminology across the SKU Price dataset, its appendix, and its supported features
2855.author: ijurica
2855.summary: ijurica opened this issue on 11 November 2026 to align pricing terms across the SKU Price dataset, its appendix and supported features, after a TF-2 update flagged several meanings of rate. Some edits may change what a requirement applies to, such as IsGlobalScope in #2735, so the author wants those flagged separately in the pull request, and lines overlapping open PR #2845 left alone. For FOCUS data users the effect would be clearer wording, with a few requirements possibly shifting in scope. The thread has no comments yet, so the group's view is unknown. No pull request exists yet.

2856.title: [AI] Clarify distinction between `SKU Price` construct and `SKU Price` records
2856.author: ijurica
2856.summary: ijurica opened this issue on 11 November 2026 to question the shared name SKU Price, used for both the construct identified by SKU Price ID and the dataset whose rows are records, where one ID spans several records. The case is that the dataset name implies one row per SKU Price, unlike Contract Commitment, and that normative requirements need the word record to avoid ambiguity, which has already caused confusion in the specification. Options are keeping the name, renaming only the dataset, or renaming it along with record-level columns such as SkuPriceEffectiveStart, since renaming the dataset alone would not change those. A rename would touch the dataset, columns, examples and preview notes, and is possible because the dataset is still preview. No one has replied yet, so the group's view is unknown.

2860.title: [AI] Add semantic tag tooling to the specification build

Tags such as column and term references are resolved to today's link and italics conventions and checked; the registry and resolver come with tests. The change is meant to be backwards compatible: with no tags the output stays identical, and tagged and hand-written links can coexist. Converting the specification would follow in separate reviewable steps, each recording conversion progress per tag kind. Two open decisions are flagged, on tool location and whether spec.md resolves tags before Pandoc; the description cuts off there. Opened 12 November 2026 and marked critical path. 2861.title: [AI] Decide the conversion and rendering rules for semantic tags
2861.author: finops-DaveMoreau
2861.summary: Opened by finops-DaveMoreau on 12 November 2026 under #2779, this issue writes down the rules for converting the specification to semantic tags, so the Working Group approves each rule once rather than reviewing 300-plus files line by line. Conversion rules decide which text becomes which tag; rendering rules decide how tags appear in the published specification, so they touch every tag. Translations carry over existing markup, wrong links included, and account for 6,841 tags in 332 files. Inferences go further: plain Display Name matching adds 866 tags in 231 files, with Title Case words meaning a concept rather than a column as the main risk. Each rule becomes a separate converter switch, and later conversion PRs would be checked only against approved rules. Nobody has commented yet, so there is no reaction to read; the issue depends on #2860.

2862.title: [AI] Convert existing references to semantic tags with the translation rules
2862.author: finops-DaveMoreau
2862.summary: finops-DaveMoreau proposes running the translation rules approved in #2861 over the specification, converting entity links, italic glossary terms and plain entity IDs into semantic tags and marking each kind as mechanical so CI keeps it converted. The conversion copies what the markup says now and corrects nothing. A first mention that will link to the glossary rather than the record #2735 describes is left for a separate change. The proposal is one PR for every kind and file, timed with maintainers, with one PR per area as the alternative. It changes 689 rendered lines but no visible words, and leaves 234 items open, mostly ColumnIds defined in several datasets. Checks show no errors and 20 warnings that reflect existing source disagreements. The thread is new, opened 12 November 2026 and assigned to TF-Supporting, with no discussion or reaction yet.

2871.title: FR #2521: Add context-window pricing properties to SKU Price Details
2871.author: jerrysr99
2871.summary:

It builds on FR #2521 and a 10 November Task Force 1 direction, with the SKU Price columns in #2872.

2872.title: FR #2521: Add context-window pricing columns to SKU Price (stacked on the properties PR)
2872.author: jerrysr99
2872.summary: jerrysr99 has opened this draft implementing the SKU Price part of FR #2521, which asks for long-context AI charges to be distinguished from standard-context charges for the same model. Google's Gemini models price at a 200K-token prompt threshold, and FOCUS data currently blends those rates together. The pull request adds two Conditional columns, ContextWindowMinimum (exclusive) and ContextWindowMaximum (inclusive), measured in input tokens per request, along with an IncludesContextWindowPricing condition, dataset requirements and an appendix example. Unlike Quantity Tier Minimum, the minimum is null when price does not vary by window size. It is stacked on #2871 and needs that branch first. Trial merges conflict with #2748, #2749 and #2753, which also edit the SKU Price column table. No reviews or approvals exist yet; the only other activity is jerrysr99's comment listing providers with context-window pricing.

2879.title: Add Azure practitioner scenarios to SKU Price supported features

The benchmark would become unfiltered SPY for every portfolio, citing a 17 November 2026 sync; the comparison script still uses filtered SPY until approval. 2881.title: AI #2783: Skip null values in the 1.5 CommitmentDiscount allowed-values rules

2881.summary: Matt-Cowsert's draft pull request fixes the 1.5 Requirements Model defect reported in #2783. The Status and Category allowed-values rules have no condition, so nulls fail them, even though the spec and C-003-C say null is correct without a commitment discount. The 1.2 to 1.4 models have the same defect but are unchanged, since those versions are published and that question sits in #2864.
